subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Should OpenClaw pursue first-class org/team deployment in core, and which security boundary should be accepted first: scaffold/docs-only, per-session tool policy, tenant isolation, or conversation identity?
rationale: The requested feature crosses core configuration, Gateway auth/session semantics, agent tool access, and documented trust boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product and security contract safely.

options.title: Keep umbrella and decompose
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broad umbrella and require maintainer-sponsored sub-issues or RFCs for each accepted security/config surface.

options.title: Narrow to docs and scaffolding
options.body: Limit core work to safer workspace scaffolding and org deployment documentation while leaving RBAC and tenant isolation to separate RFCs.

options.title: Supersede with focused security issues
options.body: Close this umbrella only after maintainers explicitly choose one canonical focused issue for each remaining scaffold, RBAC, identity, and manifest slice.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and decompose
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broad umbrella and require maintainer-sponsored sub-issues or RFCs for each accepted security/config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is recent ownership of the agent CLI/config surface and the docs that define the current Gateway trust model.
